note: The gates below are real measurements, not a count of ticked boxes in a runbook. A checkbox measures whether somebody ticked a checkbox; these read the thing itself.

verdict_template.unassured: Nothing measurable is stopping a tag, but {unassured} of {total} of the launch gates are checked by a person and nobody has looked.

goals.statement: We can say what the next release gives a player, and every one of those claims traces to the build.
goals.statement_short: we cannot say what the next release actually offers a player
goals.why_it_matters: This is the inventory. Without it Sales has nothing to take to a player, a storefront or a press contact — and the only number the wall could show was a commit count, which is how much work happened rather than what any of it gives anybody.

path_to_green.narrative: Every feature the release claims has to resolve to something in the history or to a project carrying it. One that resolves to neither is a wish on a release plan.

action.label: Put it on Victor's list
action.title: Reconcile the release manifest against the build
action.ask: A feature on hq/data/releases.json's manifest cannot be traced to a commit or to a project carrying it. Work out whether it was built under a different name, is genuinely not built, or should come off the release, and fix the record either way. A release plan whose contents cannot be verified is a wish.
action.first_action: Open #/pillar/sales, find the feature marked not built, and trace its evidence id through git log.

goals.statement: We have some signal of what players actually want, so a release can be argued for rather than guessed at.
goals.statement_short: nothing anywhere records what a player has asked for
goals.why_it_matters: Sales is supposed to work backwards from demand: hear what people want, push for it, ship it, tell them it landed. Not one of those four is possible here. There is no channel, no analytics, no wishlist and no recorded request — so every feature in the manifest was chosen on taste alone. That may be exactly right for a game this early, but it should be a choice rather than the only option available.

path_to_green.narrative: One record of what players ask for, however thin — the itch page's comments, the green tester's session notes, anything said out loud. Today the studio cannot hear anything, so the first release with an audience teaches us nothing.

action.label: Put it on Victor's list
action.title: Give the studio somewhere to record what players ask for
action.ask: Nothing in this repo records a single thing a player has wanted. Sales is meant to work backwards from demand and cannot: there is no channel, no analytics and no wishlist. Design the thinnest honest record — hq/data/demand.json — one entry per thing somebody actually asked for, with who said it and where, so a feature can eventually be argued for rather than chosen on taste alone. Do not invent entries to fill it; an empty file that is honestly empty is the correct first state. This depends on Finance & Ops' open ruling about where a player's bug report lands, so read that first.
action.first_action: Read ITCH_PAGE.md, hq/data/goals/ops.json's a-player-can-reach-us goal, and the playtest session notes, then propose the record's shape.

goals.statement: The release pipeline refuses to publish a build the runbook says is not shippable.
goals.statement_short: nothing would stop a tag shipping the debug readout
goals.why_it_matters: The runbook's checks are checkboxes in a document. The playtest readout is on right now — correctly, we are playtesting — and it only has to be off at the moment a tag is cut. That is exactly the moment nobody is watching a checklist, and release.yml checks none of it. We are one distracted tag away from shipping four lines of English into a game whose whole promise is that there is nothing to read.

measure.label: the release workflow checks the playtest readout before it publishes
measure.says_true: the release workflow refuses to publish with the readout on
measure.says_false: the release workflow publishes without checking the readout at all

path_to_green.narrative: Add a step to the release workflow that fails the tag if ui/hud.gd still says the readout is on. Half an hour, once, and the checkbox stops depending on somebody remembering.

action.label: Put it on Lena's list
action.ask: Add a guard step to .github/workflows/release.yml that fails the release before the export if ui/hud.gd's PLAYTEST_NOTES is still true. docs/DEPLOY.md's pre-release checklist names this as a manual box; it is a one-line grep and it is the only item on that list that can be enforced mechanically. Do not change the constant itself — it is deliberately on during playtesting, and the point is that the pipeline catches it at tag time rather than that it is off today. While you are there, check whether the credits-screen item can be guarded the same way.
action.first_action: Read docs/DEPLOY.md's 'Before any release' section and .github/workflows/release.yml, then add the guard step ahead of the export.
action.title: Make the release workflow enforce the pre-release checklist

goals.statement: We release often enough that the public build is never far out of date.
goals.statement_short: it has been a long time since anything was released
goals.why_it_matters: The standing ruling is ship early and often, and this is the only number that says whether we are doing it. Measured in days rather than commits: at this repo's pace a commit bar would demand a release every day and a half, which is a bar that can only ever be red.

path_to_green.narrative: The next tag is Player Update 1, and it is waiting on the onboarding gate closing.

goals.statement: The credits screen exists and opens — the attribution we owe actually ships.
goals.statement_short: the credits screen the licence depends on is not wired up
goals.why_it_matters: One shipped asset is attribution-required. If the screen carrying that attribution does not open in the build, the release is not licence-clean, whatever the ledger says.

measure.label: a credits screen is wired into the title menu
measure.says_false: no credits screen is wired into the title menu

path_to_green.narrative: Wire the credits screen before the tag.

goals.statement: A release can be built by the runbook rather than from memory.
goals.statement_short: the export configuration a release needs is missing

path_to_green.narrative: Everything the runbook needs is in the repo.

goals.statement: Somebody played the actual web build end to end before it went out.
goals.statement_short: nobody has played the web build this release would ship
goals.why_it_matters: The runbook's first line, and the one nothing can automate: sound has to arrive after the first tap, and only a person in a browser can tell you it did.

measure.reason: Playing a build is a human act. No file records that anyone did it, so the box in the runbook measures only whether somebody ticked a box.
measure.would_need: An attestation keyed to the tag being cut — your yes, dated, expiring with each release rather than standing forever.

path_to_green.narrative: Ten minutes in a browser on the exported build, before the tag.

Design the smallest honest record: an attestation keyed to the tag being cut, so it expires with each release instead of standing forever, and wire it into the launch check on the Sales & Platforms page.

goals.statement: Something checks that the game still looks the way it did before the release.
goals.statement_short: the visual check our own docs promise is run by nobody
goals.why_it_matters: The command is in the repo's own instructions. It is in no CI workflow and in no runnable job here — a check we claim and nothing runs is worse than one we never claimed.

measure.reason: tools/test_visuals.tscn needs a display, so it is in no CI workflow and in no job on the Engineering page. Nothing has ever run it on a schedule.
measure.would_need: Either a headless renderer in CI, or a job button here that a person presses before a tag — and a ruling on which.

path_to_green.narrative: Decide whether the visual check is a release gate or a developer's tool. If it is a gate it needs a home; today it has neither.

A check our own docs claim and nothing runs is worse than one we never claimed.
